suggestions.quote: This has happened before. For real. In 1324, a king from Mali, Mansa Musa, gave away so much gold in Cairo that gold stayed cheap there for at least twelve years (c06). Your gifts do it to bread. Ask Jonas.
suggestions.fix: This has happened before. For real. In 1324, a king from Mali, Mansa Musa, gave away so much gold in Cairo that gold stayed cheap there for at least twelve years (c06). Your gifts do that to the price of bread. Ask Jonas.

suggestions.quote: A king, a chessboard. One grain on the first square, and double on every square after (c05). By the last square, the board owes more wheat than the whole world grows in over a thousand years (c11).
suggestions.fix: A king, a chessboard. One grain on the first square, and double on every square after (c05). By the last square, the board owes more wheat than the whole world grows in over fourteen hundred years (c11).

suggestions.quote: Day fifty-five. The number passes what the whole world makes in a year. Every loaf, every car, every hour of work on Earth. About 128 trillion dollars (c09).
suggestions.fix: Day fifty-five. The number passes what the whole world makes in a year. Every loaf, every car, every hour of work on Earth. About 128 trillion dollars (c09). In euros, you have even more than that.

keep.quote: Ask people to carry on a doubling, and most guess far too low (c08). You just did. In public. With a band.
Never hit zero, and by day two hundred and sixty-seven your account holds more cents than the estimated number of hydrogen atoms in the observable universe (c12).
